title: GhostGrad layernorm offset scratchpad
content:
Background and symptom summary:

This is a personal scratchpad collecting everything about a recurring, intermittent NaN/Inf/huge-loss failure we see in the int8 serving path when we use BF16 weight storage + per-channel scale quantization. The failure manifests only in the production-ish binary (ONNX -> custom int8 kernels) and is NOT reproducible on pure FP32/BF16 training runs. Repro window is narrow: ~1 in 2000 requests for a single large LLM, more frequent under certain prompt patterns (long prompt + many prefix tokens).

High-level hypothesis (current):
- A combination of small LayerNorm epsilon, asymmetric per-channel scales from PTQ, and accumulation rounding in the int8 custom matmul causes tiny negative values to appear in the variance accumulator leading to sqrt(neg) -> NaN downstream in LayerNorm. These NaNs are then amplified by subsequent attention softmax or gated activations, causing exploding values and model output NaNs.
- Secondary: an export mismatch in ONNX for layernorm mean/var semantics (order of subtraction vs accumulation) that interacts badly with quantized int8 accumulator saturations.

What we observe (concrete):
- Seen on A100, T4 inference fleets. Not device-specific.
- Traceback from the serving binary (trimmed):
  [inference-worker] runtime/quant_kernel.cc:523 compute_layernorm_variance: CHECK(!isnan(var)) failed: var is NaN
  [worker] request_id=9a2c: model returned NaN logits -> request aborted
- In a couple of repro attempts I dumped intermediate activations (pre-layernorm) and saw very small negative values in the variance accumulator (values like -1e-14 to -1e-12) prior to sqrt. Those numbers would be zero in FP32 path but ended up negative after int8->accumulate conversion and rounding.

Commands + experimental harness used so far:
- Export path: torch -> onnx (opset 17) using export_with_dynamic_axes True, special handling for layernorm (custom op fallback)
- Run with onnxruntime CPU EP: "python tools/onnx_run.py --model model.onnx --input sample.json --ep cpu" -> stable, no NaN
- Run with custom int8 runtime: "./bin/serve --model model.int8.onnx --profile flint --backend fastint --calib-table calib.json" -> intermittent NaN
- Calibration collection: "python scripts/collect_calib.py --dataset wikitext --samples 1024 --per-channel" (we switched between per-tensor and per-channel; per-channel shows more NaNs)
- Small local reproducer: instrumented forward across 5 seeds to try to get NaN deterministically. Seed-dependent: sometimes shows up with seed 1729 only when input length > 2048 tokens.

Micro-bisect notes (runs):
- run-20251124-A: FP32 baseline -> no NaN, loss ~ 1.1
- run-20251201-B: ONNX FP32 -> no NaN, loss ~ 1.12 (close)
- run-20260105-C: ONNX int8 per-tensor scales -> rare NaN (1/10k)
- run-20260118-D: ONNX int8 per-channel scales -> NaN rate up to 1/2k
- run-20260220-E: int8 with layernorm epsilon forced to 1e-5 (was 1e-12) -> NaN rate dropped to near zero

Quick debugging traces (tensor prints):
- dump at layernorm variance acc (signed 64-bit accumulate) after gemm:
  idx: 0 val: 1.234567e-05
  idx: 1 val: 9.876543e-06
  idx: 2 val: -1.2345e-12  <-- tiny negative
  idx: 3 val: 8.765432e-06
- After cast back to float and dividing by N-1: idx 2 becomes -3.1e-18 -> sqrt -> NaN in runtime due to check that converts denormals wrongly in custom sqrt impl.

What changed recently (possible triggers):
- Deployment of new int8 kernel optimizer (vectorized accumulation) in PR 942 (linked above). That changed accumulation ordering and introduced a fast path that casts accumulators to BF16 intermediate to exploit TensorCores. Suspect loss of exact associativity increased rounding noise.
- Calib script change to per-channel symmetric quant instead of per-tensor; improved accuracy but introduced scale ranges that are tiny for some channels (scale < 1e-4). Small scales -> large inverse multipliers -> underflow/overflow in intermediate staging.

Hypotheses (detailed):
1) Denormal/underflow interaction: The int8->bf16 intermediate path produces denormals during accumulation; our fast sqrt impl handles denormals incorrectly (treats them as signaling NaN) -> failure.
2) LayerNorm epsilon too small in int8 path: model uses eps=1e-12 optimized for FP32; when quantized, variance estimates occasionally fall below eps due to rounding, causing negative values after subtract with mean -> NaN. Forcing eps to 1e-5 fixed most cases in test harness.
3) Calibration outliers: per-channel scales estimated from small calibration set produce an extremely small scale for rarely-activated channels; quantization then amplifies tiny floating drift to negative variance.
4) Export semantic mismatch: ONNX op for layernorm might be expressed as var = sum(x^2)/N - mean^2 or as (1/N)sum((x-mean)^2); different evaluation ordering can change rounding pattern. Our custom kernel expects ordering B but export used A.

Things tried already (and outcomes):
- Increase layernorm eps (1e-12 -> 1e-5): massive drop in NaN (good) but potential small accuracy delta on perplexity (+0.4%). Needs perf/regression check.
- Switch calibs to per-tensor symmetric: NaN rate decreased dramatically (suggests per-channel extremes are suspect) but token-level quality degraded for some prompts.
- Revert accumulation ordering to scalar slow path (no BF16 intermediate): NaNs disappear (but performance drops ~20%).
- Add post-accum clamp: clamp variance accumulator to >= 0 before sqrt; fixed NaN but uncomfortable as a band-aid.
- Add denormal flush to zero (FTZ) in kernel: mitigates but not fully deterministic across devices.

Open experiments to run next (actionable checklist):
- [ ] Run long-running fuzz harness (100k inferences) with eps=1e-6, 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-5 to find sweet spot between stability and accuracy. Capture perplexity on heldout.
- [ ] Re-run calibration with larger sample (10k) to see if tiny per-channel scales persist.
- [ ] Add assertion/logging in export that prints layernorm op implementation chosen by ONNX graph (compare sum(x^2)/N vs mean-based path).
- [ ] Add fallback: if var < 1e-9 after accumulation, recompute variance in FP32 slow-path for that layer for this batch only (costly but targeted). Measure frequency.
- [ ] Check PR 942 for any cast-to-bf16 sites and try a branch that keeps accumulation in int32 before BF16 cast; run A/B.
- [ ] Instrument the runtime to capture distribution of per-channel scales (histogram) and log any scale < 1e-5.

Longer-term design options (notes):
- Consider pinned layernorm kernels for quantized path that are numerically robust (Kahan or compensated summation) at expense of some cycles.
- Add quantization-time regularizer that forbids channels with scale below threshold; instead force per-tensor fallback. This keeps quality but avoids pathological small scales.
- Add model-side hygiene: training with small noise injection or adding a min-variance hook to layernorm to make it robust to quantization noise.

Random small observations / fragments to keep: (brain dump)
- The failure often correlates with long prefix tokens containing many identical repeated tokens (e.g., 'the the the ...') — possible pathological activation sparsity leading to tiny variance.
- We saw one image where the pre-LN vector had almost identical values except one entry that was -1e-6, that single negative moved variance calc to slightly negative after rounding.
- Possible quick experiment: replace layernorm with rmsnorm in the int8 path for test — RMS uses sum(x^2) only and may be less sensitive to mean subtraction rounding order.

Slack notes / who to ping:
- Ping Jin Park (kernel owner) to check PR 942 performance vs numerical guarantees.
- Ping Maya Ortiz for calibration dataset increase and perf tradeoffs.
- Flag SRE/ops if we decide to push eps change in production.

Immediate safe mitigation for prod (proposal):
- Deploy kernel change that clamps var to max(var, 1e-10) right before sqrt + add warning counter. This is low-risk and resolved customer incidents in staging. Plan to monitor token-level fallback counts and quality regressions.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after running fuzz harness and PR test branch.

Notes last updated 2026-03-05 by Ava.
